supabase_conn_from_this_mac.title: Connecting to Supabase Postgres from this Mac: direct host is IPv6-only, use the pooler
supabase_conn_from_this_mac.content:
Verified 2026-09-03 while wiring ~/Projects/edu-os to its Supabase project.

1. **The direct host does not work from this machine.** `db.<ref>.supabase.co` resolves to an AAAA record only (e.g. `2406:da18:...`); psql fails with `could not translate host name ... nodename nor servname provided`. Do not debug DNS — go straight to the session pooler.
2. **Pooler host = `aws-0-ap-southeast-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432` (Singapore)** for the Edu OS project. Username becomes `postgres.<project-ref>`, not `postgres`. Guessing the region by latitude is wrong — ap-south-1 (Mumbai) returned `FATAL: (ENOTFOUND) tenant/user postgres.<ref> not found`. When the region is unknown, probe it:
   ```bash
   for h in aws-0-ap-southeast-1 aws-1-ap-southeast-1 aws-0-us-east-1 aws-1-us-east-1 aws-0-eu-central-1 aws-0-ap-south-1; do
     r=$(/usr/local/opt/postgresql@17/bin/psql "postgresql://postgres.<ref>:<pw>@$h.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres?connect_timeout=6" -tAc "select current_database();" 2>&1 | head -1)
     echo "$h :: $r"; case "$r" in postgres) echo ">>> MATCH $h"; break;; esac
   done
   ```
   A wrong region errors instantly with `tenant/user not found`; the right one returns `postgres`.
3. **URL-encode the password.** A `#` truncates the connection string — write it `%23`. Same for `@` (`%40`), `/` (`%2F`), `:` (`%3A`).
4. Append `?connection_limit=5` for Prisma against the pooler.
5. **There is no GNU `timeout` on this Mac** (`command not found`). Use the libpq `?connect_timeout=N` parameter instead of wrapping psql in `timeout`.
6. Homebrew psql 17.9 lives at `/usr/local/opt/postgresql@17/bin/psql` — `postgresql@17` is the running brew service; the bare `psql` on PATH is 14.21. Use the explicit @17 path for anything touching a v17 server.

Credentials are not recorded here — the Edu OS DB password was pasted into a transcript and told to be rotated. Read it from `~/Projects/edu-os/.env`.

edu_os_project_foundation.title: Edu OS — foundation decisions, layout, and the single-analytics-source rule
edu_os_project_foundation.content:
Greenfield build started 2026-09-03 at `~/Projects/edu-os` for the Alibaba Cloud AI Hackathon 2026 (Bano Qabil × Alkhidmat, Education track). Grand finale 2026-09-10. Three developers: Basim, Shan, Muneeb. Plan: `~/.claude/plans/edu-os-memoized-minsky.md`.

**Deliberately separate from the live GSS apps.** It is NOT the "Idara / Zehen" concept in `~/Projects/alibaba-hackathon-2026/EDU-OS.md`, which federates the seven production Ghazali school systems. Edu OS is self-contained, 100% synthetic data, own repo, own DB, zero coupling to the shared GSS Supabase or any real student record. Bano Qabil is only the demo persona — never claim the synthetic rows are real Bano Qabil records.

**Stack (user-chosen, do not re-litigate):** one Next.js 15 App Router app, TypeScript, Prisma 6, Tailwind v4 (`@theme` block in globals.css, no tailwind.config), Recharts. Layout: `app/(app)|(auth)|api`, `components/{ui,app}`, `lib/`, `lib/ai/{client,guard,tools,context,prompts}`, `prisma/`, `scripts/`.

**`lib/analytics.ts` is the single source of truth for every performance number.** Performance is computed, never stored. Every dashboard, API route, report, and AI context builder must import from it (`instituteSummary`, `coursePerformance`, `batchPerformance`, `instructorPerformance`, `moduleWeakness`, `skillLevelFromScore`, …). Nothing else may invent a formula — otherwise the same batch shows three different scores on three screens built by three developers. Enforce this in every subagent prompt that touches the app.

**AI layer:** Qwen via DashScope-intl OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`, `qwen-plus`), with the api-engine gateway as fallback. **No `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` exists on this machine** — every AI feature has a deterministic non-AI fallback and `AI_ENABLED=false` must keep the app working. AI must never fabricate students, scores, attendance, or statistics; if data is missing it says "Insufficient data available for this analysis."

**Data:** schema pushed and seeded to Supabase (see the pooler memory). 24 skills, 8 courses, 45 modules, 15 instructors, 240 students, 12 batches, 300 enrollments, 5,540 attendance rows, 900 submissions, 900 assessment results, 1,328 derived student skills. Demo logins, password `password`: `student@eduos.pk` (Ali Hassan, batch PY-12), `instructor@eduos.pk` (Kamran Aziz), `admin@eduos.pk` (Shahid Mehmood).

**Verification:** `scripts/smoke.mjs [baseUrl]` logs in as all three roles and renders every page, failing on a Server Component crash — a crashed RSC still returns 200, so status codes alone prove nothing. Also `npm run check` (consistency) and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

**Out of scope permanently:** AI Early Warning System, AI Action Recommendation System. Do not reintroduce them.

refinements.trigger: Persist two local memories: the Supabase-from-this-Mac connection procedure (IPv6-only direct host, pooler region probe, %23 password encoding) and the Edu OS project foundation facts including the single-source-of-truth analytics rule.
refinements.evidence: Both are backed by direct trajectory evidence. (1) Connecting to the Supabase project cost four failed attempts: `db.rcftjcmariirhvvaoraa.supabase.co` resolved only to an AAAA record and failed with 'could not translate host name'; the assumed ap-south-1 pooler returned 'tenant/user not found'; the working host (`aws-0-ap-southeast-1.pooler.supabase.com`) was only found by probing regions in a loop; and the `#` in the password had to be URL-encoded as `%23`. `timeout` also does not exist on this Mac, so `?connect_timeout=N` was the workaround. Any future session touching this DB would repeat that whole search. (2) Edu OS was scaffolded this session with decisions that later sessions and the two other developers must not re-litigate — repo location, stack, Supabase as the shared DB, seeded demo logins, the missing DashScope key, and above all `lib/analytics.ts` as the only place a performance number may be computed (the whole reason six parallel agents could build three surfaces without contradicting each other). Nothing global is proposed; both entries are project/environment facts for this work. The Supabase password is deliberately not recorded — the user was told to rotate it.
refinements.outcome: A future session working on Edu OS connects to the shared Postgres on the first try, does not re-derive the pooler region or the URL-encoding gotcha, and does not introduce a second performance formula outside lib/analytics.ts. Validate by running `/usr/local/opt/postgresql@17/bin/psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c 'select current_database();'` from ~/Projects/edu-os and by grepping for any performance math outside lib/analytics.ts.
